metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent clicked the system tray icon, used the volume slider in the GNOME system tray menu to drag it all the way to the right (max/100%), then dismissed the menu.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open system tray menu, locate and manipulate the volume slider to a target level
metadata.explanation: Hardened from the original max-volume task by changing the target to 50%. Evaluator runs pactl get-sink-volume and checks the percentage string is within ±5% of 50, ensuring a different slider position than the original is required. [Fixed: renamed getter/metric MD5 suffix from invalid 8-char 'be652a00' to valid 32-char '2ac92884cbfeefbd5a2d6929c20839d7']
metadata.task_rationale: Same setup and interaction family (system tray volume slider), different numeric target. Initial state (low/some volume) will not pass the 50% check unless the agent adjusts to the correct position.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly uses 'pactl get-sink-volume @DEFAULT_SINK@', the standard PulseAudio command for checking current volume level on Ubuntu/GNOME desktops.
Metric correctly parses the first percentage value from pactl output using regex and checks abs(actual - 50) <= 5, which directly verifies the 'turn down to 50%' instruction.
Tolerance of ±5% is appropriate for a slider-based UI interaction.
Negative control resistance is sound: an unchanged high volume (e.g., 100%) will produce abs(100-50)=50 > 5, correctly returning 0.0.
Evaluator covers the single requirement in the instruction with no missing checks.
